question: The model asks to read a file inside the project. That file is a link to a file outside it. What does the wall do?

options.text: In the model, which should know better.
options.why: Tempting and wrong. The model can ask for anything; the harness must check it.

options.text: In Workspace.path(), which compares the resolved path with the project root.
options.why: Right. Joining an absolute path replaces the project folder, and the check catches the result.

options.text: In run_command, which blocks absolute paths in shell commands.
options.why: Tempting. run_command is a different tool; read_file and edit_file call the same path check.

question: Where does an absolute path such as /etc/hosts get stopped?

options.text: All of it, because the model needs every line.

question: Why does the wall call resolve() before it checks the path?

options.text: The path check in Workspace.path(), which runs on every command.
options.why: Tempting. The check runs on the paths the file tools receive. A shell command is not split into paths for it.

options.text: Nothing in this step. The wall guards the file tools, and only the gate in step 4 or the operating system's sandbox closes a shell.
options.why: Right. A shell can open any path a command names, and the wall does not see the command.
